title: Louis Armstrong, Velma Middleton and the Newport tribute
summary: She first heard Louis at a ballroom dance and calls him the greatest. She cannot recall what she sang at George Wein's televised Armstrong tribute, which also had Dizzy Gillespie.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: without, we don't want to do a whole interview without even mentioning Louie. I mean, where did you ever even hear Louie for instance?
At a ballroom dance.
And didn't that knock you right back on your heels?
Yeah. You just know he's the greatest and that's that.
Yeah.
And Velma (Middleton). And, what's that first he had before Velma? She was a good friend of mine. I can't think of her name.
I don't know who was before Velma.
She was a big fat light girl.
Really?
And she used to dance and go down in them splits and things.
Really, I don't know. I just remember Velma.
Her name will come to me.
Well if there ever was a performer, Louie was it, wasn't he?
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Oh yes. He was the great one.

He sure was. And on that subject Helen, I remember seeing you on T.V. on a tribute to Louie which George Wein had put on. It was Newport or something. It was televised. What did you sing, I can't remember what you sang? I remember Dizzy was on it.
Yeah.
And they had a nice shot of you. They gave you quite alot of time.
They did.
You don't remember?
I can't remember what I sang.
You must have sung something I suppose that tied up with Louie in some sort of way. It wasn't "Sleepy Town Down South" or anything, was it?
It wasn't "Sleepy Town Down South", no. Was it "Mood Indigo"? No.
Well, it doesn't matter. I just thought you might remember.
No, I don't remember.
But that was out there on Long Island at that big thing, wasn't it?
S. & S. REPORTING COMPANY, INC. WOrth 2-2915 WOrth 2-2943
Oh yeah.
